summary: Second independent review of the preparation/failure-classification fixes and the R1/R2 runtime evidence at e2936a898; this is not final performance acceptance and R3 (job 43987249) results still need an independent review. The code matches the agreed scope: common.condition resets only the five owned files, runs the sequential warmer under numactl --interleave=all, allows at most eight missing-page repair passes (range(1,9)), keeps the gate at zero resident pages (cold) and >=99.9% per file (warm), persists every reset/prepared/repair snapshot plus memory_before/after to JF_CACHE_REPORT on both pass and fail paths, and raises CacheGateError only for the final threshold check; eviction failures, subprocess failures and invalid kinds raise plain errors that abort. Conditioning runs inside begin() before the start barrier, so it is untimed. bench.py catches CacheGateError on rank 0 only, writes the cache-unavailable record and calls comm.Abort(42); read.py does the same with SystemExit(42); common.cache_unavailable refuses non-warm settings, so a cold gate failure still aborts via the outer handler. campaign.execute accepts rc 0 + status pass, or rc 42 + status cache-unavailable + warm + not preflight, records gib_s=None for skipped cases, and writes complete.json as 'partial' when any case is not pass; the initial Weka probe catches only CacheGateError. audit.py now enforces conditioning.kind (JFRC-05), requires root-cleanup.json (JFRC-03), and its unavailable() path refuses any rate/measurement, requires status fail/kind warm, exactly ten history entries ending at repair-8, and at least one file below threshold; completion status must equal partial iff any case was unavailable. run.sbatch adds --signal=B:TERM@180, EXIT/TERM/INT traps that forward TERM to the campaign, wait, remove the whole private root and write root-cleanup.json with the exit code; campaign.py converts SIGTERM to SystemExit so its finally block removes the xtc copy (JFRC-01 resolved for catchable signals; SIGKILL remains uncatchable as documented). test_launcher.py exercises the actual run.sbatch text with a harmless child in normal and TERM modes and tests.log shows all fifteen tests passing. DataSource/KvikIO settings, counts (50000 reads, 335571760000 bytes), 20-case matrix and 6 GiB budget are unchanged; the input adapter is unchanged. Evidence: R1 (code 1e526c602, sdfampere038) progress.json/cold JSON show zero initial residency, 335571760000 bytes, loop 55.64 s, 5.6168 GiB/s, NIC RX 359400668221 bytes over 57.56 s on one interface, cleanup.json removed=true, and the warm log confirms the old gate failed without a residency vector. R2 (code 13e576f33, sdfampere032) preparation-probe.cache.json confirms the per-file sequence (s009 81.74% -> 95.55% -> 98.26% -> 99.09%, other files stable), interleave policy active across NUMA nodes 0-7, status fail with the full vector persisted, and both cleanup.json and root-cleanup.json record removal with exit code 1; no R2 rates exist. Remaining findings are non-blocking: untested propagation of MPI abort code 42 through mpiexec (fail-closed if wrong), a tight 90-minute budget given nine full rewarm cycles, a TERM-during-staging cleanup delay, a test that does not pin the exception type, incomplete R2/R3 submission records, and minor auditor robustness gaps.

findings.evidence: Rank 0 writes the cache-unavailable record then calls comm.Abort(42); campaign.execute (campaign.py:57) accepts the case as unavailable only if completed.returncode==42. The mapping of MPI_Abort errorcode to the mpiexec/prterun exit status is not covered by any test in the tree; the only runtime data point is R1's Errorcode 1 producing exit status 1 (psana-weka-b1-warm-r1.log, 43983799.err). If prterun returned a different status for 42, require() would abort the whole campaign at the first unavailable psana warm case. This is fail-closed (no false pass) but would waste the R3 allocation.
findings.requested_change: In the final R3 review, confirm from the case .log and progress.json that any psana cache-unavailable case exited with status 42. For future reruns add a CPU-only regression test that launches mpiexec -n 1 with a script calling MPI.COMM_WORLD.Abort(42) and asserts returncode 42, or have campaign.execute also accept the documented JSON status when returncode is non-zero and the .cache.json records status fail with repair-8 (still never a rate).

findings.evidence: --time=01:30:00 with --signal=B:TERM@180. The campaign performs ten full reset+interleaved rewarm cycles of 313 GiB (one probe, six Weka warm cases, three local warm cases), each allowing up to eight repair passes. The R2 probe needed 322 s for one prepare plus three repairs on Weka (preparation-probe.cache.json seconds=322.25); R1 needed about 10 minutes for staging, hashing, two preflights and one cold case. Nine cold cases, nine warm loops and a per-case 1200 s cap add further time. The aggregate plausibly approaches or exceeds 5400 s if Weka repairs run long, in which case the TERM path removes the stage and leaves no complete.json; the auditor refuses, so the outcome is fail-closed but the retry is lost.
findings.requested_change: No change to the running job. For the final review, record elapsed wall time and per-case conditioning_seconds from progress.json; if the job ends by TERM, report it as an incomplete campaign and do not derive any rate. For any future rerun, drop the redundant initial probe or request a longer allocation rather than reducing repairs or thresholds.

findings.evidence: with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as ex: staged=list(ex.map(copy_one,paths(SOURCE))). If SIGTERM arrives during staging, the handler raises SystemExit inside the with block, but ThreadPoolExecutor.__exit__ calls shutdown(wait=True) and blocks until all five in-flight 50-73 GB copies finish. The 180 s grace before Slurm's SIGKILL would be exceeded, so neither cleanup.json nor root-cleanup.json would be written. Likelihood is low because TERM@180 arrives near the end of the allocation, not during the first minutes.
findings.requested_change: Optional for reruns: set a threading.Event in the SIGTERM handler and check it inside the copy_one read loop (raise to stop the copy), or call ex.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) from the handler, so finally can remove the partial stage within the grace window.

findings.evidence: test_failed_preparation_preserves_all_checks asserts assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'Cache gate failed'). CacheGateError subclasses ValueError, so the test would still pass if common.condition regressed to raising a plain ValueError, which would silently change bench.py/read.py behaviour from 'cache-unavailable' to a full campaign abort. No test asserts that eviction or subprocess failures do NOT raise CacheGateError.
findings.requested_change: Assert common.CacheGateError explicitly, and add a negative test that a failing residency(...,True) during reset raises ValueError but not CacheGateError, plus one that a CalledProcessError from the warmer propagates unchanged.

findings.evidence: unavailable() checks history length and last stage name but does not verify that history[0]['stage']=='reset' with zero resident pages, that cache['cache'] equals history[-1]['cache'], or that the five file paths/pages match the owned input set recorded in the campaign's pass cases. It also does not enforce an upper bound on cache['seconds'] or compare the five paths against the case's --directory. These are robustness gaps; the per-file threshold check still prevents a passing cache from being labelled unavailable.
findings.requested_change: Optionally add need(cache['history'][0]['stage']=='reset' and cache['history'][0]['cache']['resident_pages']==0), need(cache['cache']==cache['history'][-1]['cache']), and need({Path(x['path']).name for x in files}==set(expected_names)) and report the five per-file fractions in unavailable_warm_cases.
